p.src: The tale tells how the Great Sage Equal to Heaven was escorted by the heavenly troops to the Demon-Beheading Terrace, where he was bound to the Demon-Subduing Pillar. Blades hacked, axes hewed, spears stabbed, and swords gouged, yet none could wound his body. The Southern Dipper stars then ordered the gods of the Fire Ministry to kindle their flames and roast him, but even they could not burn him. Next the gods of the Thunder Ministry struck him with thunderbolts, but still they could not harm so much as a single hair. The Mighty Ghost King and the others memorialized the throne: “Your Majesty, we know not where this Great Sage learned such a body-protecting art. Though your servants hacked him with blades and axes and struck him with thunder and fire, we could not injure him in the least. What are we to do?” On hearing this, the Jade Emperor said, “If the wretch is like this, how can he be dealt with?” Lord Laozi at once memorialized: “That monkey ate the immortal peaches, drank the imperial wine, and also stole the elixir pills. All five gourds of my elixir, both raw and refined, went into his belly. By working the samadhi fire within himself, he fused them into one mass, and thus his whole body became hard as adamant, so that he cannot readily be harmed. Better let this old Daoist take him away and place him in the Eight Trigrams Furnace, where civil and martial fire will refine him. Once my elixir is recovered, his body will naturally be reduced to ashes.” Hearing this, the Jade Emperor ordered the Six Ding and Six Jia gods to untie the Great Sage and hand him over to Lord Laozi. Lord Laozi received the decree and departed. Meanwhile, the Illustrious Sage Erlang was summoned and rewarded with a hundred golden flowers, a hundred bottles of imperial wine, a hundred restoration pills, rare treasures, bright pearls, brocades, and other gifts, which he was told to share with his sworn brothers. The True Lord gave thanks for the imperial favor and returned to the Mouth of the Guan River. Of him we shall speak no more.

p.src: When Lord Laozi reached the Tushita Palace, he removed the Great Sage’s bonds and released the instrument piercing his shoulder blades, then thrust him into the Eight Trigrams Furnace. He ordered the furnace attendants and fire-tending boys to fan up the flames and refine him. Now the furnace was divided according to the eight trigrams: Qian, Kan, Gen, Zhen, Xun, Li, Kun, and Dui. He slipped into the place beneath the Xun trigram. Xun signifies wind, and where there is wind, there is no fire. Yet the wind stirred up smoke, which seared his pair of eyes red and left them permanently inflamed; hence they came to be called “Fiery Eyes and Golden Pupils.”

p.src: Time truly flies. Before anyone knew it, seven times seven—forty-nine days—had passed, and Lord Laozi’s firing was complete. Then one day he opened the furnace to retrieve his elixir. The Great Sage had both hands covering his eyes and was rubbing them as tears streamed down when he suddenly heard a noise at the mouth of the furnace. He opened his eyes wide and saw the light. Unable to restrain himself, he sprang up and leapt from the alchemical furnace. With a tremendous crash he kicked over the Eight Trigrams Furnace and strode outside. The fire tenders, furnace keepers, Ding and Jia gods, and the rest rushed in alarm to seize him, but he felled every one of them, like a white-browed tiger in a fit or a one-horned dragon gone mad. Lord Laozi caught up and made a grab for him, but the Great Sage gave him a shove that sent him head over heels, then broke free and fled. He pulled the Compliant Rod from his ear and waved it into the wind. It grew as thick as a bowl, and he took it in hand as before. Striking without distinction, he once again threw Heaven into turmoil, beating the Nine Luminaries until they barred their doors and the Four Heavenly Kings until they vanished from sight. The True Lord, Guardian Sage, had already dispatched his officers with an order to the Thunder Ministry, mustering all thirty-six thunder generals. They surrounded the Great Sage at the heart of the encirclement, each displaying his ferocity in bitter combat. The Great Sage showed not the slightest fear. Wielding his Compliant Rod, he blocked on the left and parried on the right, warded off attacks from behind, and met those from the front. p.src: Having received the decree, the two sages went straight to the blessed realm of Spirit Mountain and stood before the precious monastery of the Thunderclap Temple. After paying their respects to the Four Vajra Guardians and the Eight Bodhisattvas, they asked them to convey their message. The deities went beneath the precious lotus throne and reported the matter, whereupon the Tathagata summoned the visitors. The two sages circled the Buddha three times in reverence, then stood in attendance below the throne. The Tathagata asked, “What trouble afflicts the Jade Emperor that has brought you two sages here?” The two sages replied, “Some time ago a monkey was born on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. There he displayed his magic powers, gathered a host of monkeys, and threw the world into disorder. The Jade Emperor issued a decree of amnesty and enlistment and appointed him Protector of the Horses, but he considered the office too low and rebelled. The Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King Li and Prince Nezha were sent to capture him but failed. He was offered amnesty again and appointed Great Sage Equal to Heaven, at first with title but no salary. He was put in charge of the Immortal Peach Garden, and there he stole the peaches; then he went to the Jade Pool, stole the delicacies and wine, and disrupted the great banquet; and emboldened by wine, he secretly entered the Tushita Palace, stole Lord Laozi’s elixir, and rebelled his way out of Heaven. The Jade Emperor then dispatched a hundred thousand heavenly troops, yet even they could not subdue him. Later Guanyin recommended the True Lord Erlang, who, together with his sworn brothers, pursued and fought the monkey. The creature assumed countless transformations, and only when Lord Laozi struck him with the Diamond Snare could Erlang capture him. He was escorted before the throne, and orders were given for his execution. But hacking with blades and axes, burning with fire, and striking with thunder could not harm him. Lord Laozi obtained imperial approval to take him away and refine him with fire. When the cauldron was opened after forty-nine days, however, he leapt from the Eight Trigrams Furnace, beat back the heavenly warriors, and drove straight through the Hall of Perfect Light to the outside of the Hall of Miraculous Mist. There he was stopped by Divine Officer Wang, assistant to the True Lord, Guardian Sage, and they fought bitterly. Then thirty-six thunder generals were summoned to trap him in the heart of their encirclement, but still none could approach him. The situation is desperate, and therefore the Jade Emperor has specially invited the Tathagata to save his throne.” When the Tathagata heard this, he said to the bodhisattvas, “Remain seated here peacefully in the Dharma hall. Do not disturb your places of meditation. Wait while I go subdue the demon and rescue the Emperor.”

p.src: Hearing this, the Buddha gave a cold chuckle and said, “You wretch are merely a monkey spirit. How dare you deceive yourself into thinking you can seize the honored throne of the Jade Emperor? He has cultivated himself since childhood and endured the hardships of one thousand seven hundred and fifty cosmic cycles. Each cycle lasts one hundred and twenty-nine thousand six hundred years. Calculate how many years he had to pass before he could enjoy this boundless Great Way. How can a beast like you, only newly born into the human way, utter such outrageous boasts? Shameful, utterly shameful! Such words will shorten your allotted life. Submit to the true faith while there is still time, and speak no more nonsense. Otherwise, I fear you will meet a deadly hand and lose your life in an instant, thereby ruining your original nature.” The Great Sage said, “Though he began his cultivation young and has practiced for a long time, he still ought not to occupy this place forever. As the saying goes, ‘Emperors take their turns; next year the throne comes to my house.’ Let him simply move out and yield the Heavenly Palace to me, and that will be the end of it; but if he refuses, I shall keep raising havoc, and there will never be peace.” The Buddha said, “Apart from the arts of immortality and transformation, what other abilities have you that you dare claim the blessed realm of Heaven?” The Great Sage said, “I have plenty of abilities! I possess seventy-two transformations and an immortal life that shall not age through ten thousand cycles; I can ride the Somersault Cloud and cover one hundred and eight thousand li in a single bound. Why should I not sit upon the throne of Heaven?” The Buddha said, “Let us make a wager. If you truly have the ability to somersault out of my right palm, you shall be the winner. There will be no need to raise weapons or wage bitter war: I shall invite the Jade Emperor to dwell in the West and have him yield the Heavenly Palace to you. But if you cannot escape my palm, you must return to the lower world and live as a demon, cultivate yourself for several more cycles, and only then come back to quarrel over it.” When the Great Sage heard this, he laughed inwardly: “This Tathagata is a perfect fool. Old Sun can travel one hundred and eight thousand li in a single somersault, while his palm is not even a foot across. How could I fail to leap out of it?” He promptly cried aloud, “If that is what you say, do you have the authority to decide this?” The Buddha replied, “I do, I do.” He opened his right hand, which seemed no larger than a lotus leaf.

p.src: The Great Sage put away his Compliant Rod, summoned all his divine might, and sprang into the Buddha’s palm, saying, “Off I go!” In a streak of cloud-light he sped away, leaving neither form nor shadow. Watching with his wisdom-eye, the Buddha saw the Monkey King whirl onward without pause like the vanes of a windmill. As the Great Sage traveled on, he suddenly saw five flesh-red pillars supporting a mass of blue vapor. He said, “This must be the end of the road. When I return, the Tathagata will bear witness, and the Hall of Divine Mists shall surely be mine to occupy.” Then he reconsidered: “Wait. I had better leave some mark here, so that I shall have proof when I speak with the Tathagata.” He plucked out a hair, breathed an immortal breath upon it, and cried, “Change!” It changed into a double-bristled brush heavy with ink, with which he wrote a line of large characters on the middle pillar: “The Great Sage Equal to Heaven was here.” When he had finished writing, he recovered the hair. Then, with no regard for dignity, he relieved himself at the foot of the first pillar, leaving a puddle of monkey urine. Turning his Somersault Cloud around, he went straight back to where he had begun, stood in the Tathagata’s palm, and said, “I went away and have now returned. Now tell the Jade Emperor to yield the Heavenly Palace to me.”

p.src: The Tathagata rebuked him: “You piss-reeking monkey spirit! You have never left my palm at all.” The Great Sage said, “You know nothing of it. I went to the very edge of Heaven, where I saw five flesh-red pillars supporting a mass of blue vapor. I left a mark there. Do you dare come with me to see it?” The Tathagata said, “There is no need to go. Just lower your head and look.” The Great Sage opened his Fiery Eyes and Golden Pupils wide and looked down. There, on the middle finger of the Buddha’s right hand, were written the words, “The Great Sage Equal to Heaven was here.” And from the cleft at the base of the thumb there still came the rank smell of monkey urine. The Great Sage was startled and exclaimed, “How can this be? How can this be? I wrote those words on the pillars supporting Heaven. How did they come to be on his finger? Could he possess some art of knowing things before they happen? I refuse to believe it. I do not believe it! Let me go there once more.”

p.src: What a Great Sage! He hastily sprang up, intending to leap away once more. But the Buddha overturned his palm with a single blow, thrusting the Monkey King beyond the Western Gate of Heaven. He transformed his five fingers into five connected mountains corresponding to metal, wood, water, fire, and earth, named them the Mountain of Five Elements, and lightly pinned him beneath them. The thunder gods, Ananda, and Kasyapa all pressed their palms together and proclaimed, “Excellent! Excellent!”

p.src: After the Tathagata Buddha had subdued and destroyed the demon monkey’s power, he called Ananda and Kasyapa to return with him to the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. At that moment Tianpeng and Tianyou hurried out of the Hall of Divine Mists and said, “We beg the Tathagata to wait a little. Our sovereign is coming in person.” Hearing this, the Buddha turned his head and respectfully looked back. Presently there indeed appeared a phoenix carriage adorned with the Eight Trigrams beneath a jeweled canopy of ninefold radiance. Profound songs and wondrous music sounded, countless divine hymns were chanted, precious flowers were scattered, and true fragrance filled the air. The procession came straight before the Buddha, and the Jade Emperor offered thanks, saying, “By your mighty Dharma the evil demon has been subdued. We ask the Tathagata to remain for one day while we invite the immortals to a banquet in gratitude.” The Tathagata dared not refuse. Pressing his palms together, he replied courteously, “This old monk came here at the command of the Great Celestial Worthy. What power could I claim? It was all due to the abundant blessings of the Celestial Worthy and the assembled gods. How could I presume to trouble you for thanks?” The Jade Emperor issued a decree ordering the gods of the Thunder Ministry to go separately and invite the Three Pure Ones, Four Imperial Sovereigns, Five Elders, Six Offices, Seven Primes, Eight Poles, Nine Luminaries, Ten Capitals, the thousand perfected ones, and the myriad sages to attend the gathering and join in thanking the Buddha for his grace. He also commanded the Four Great Celestial Masters and the immortal maidens of the Nine Heavens to throw open the Golden Portal of the Jade Capital, the Precious Palace of the Great Mystery, and the Jade Hall of Grottoed Light; to seat the Tathagata in honor upon the seven-jeweled sacred dais; to arrange the ranks of seats; and to prepare dragon liver, phoenix marrow, jade nectar, and immortal peaches.

u.src: After the Tathagata Buddha had subdued and destroyed the demon monkey’s power, he called Ananda and Kasyapa to return with him to the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.

ja: れいしょうたからどの
u.src: At that moment Tianpeng and Tianyou hurried out of the Hall of Divine Mists and said, “We beg the Tathagata to wait a little. Our sovereign is coming in person.”
Hearing this, the Buddha turned his head and respectfully looked back.

Presently there indeed appeared a phoenix carriage adorned with the Eight Trigrams beneath a jeweled canopy of ninefold radiance. Profound songs and wondrous music sounded, countless divine hymns were chanted, precious flowers were scattered, and true fragrance filled the air. The procession came straight before the Buddha, and the Jade Emperor offered thanks, saying, “By your mighty Dharma the evil demon has been subdued. We ask the Tathagata to remain for one day while we invite the immortals to a banquet in gratitude.”
The Tathagata dared not refuse. Pressing his palms together, he replied courteously, “This old monk came here at the command of the Great Celestial Worthy. What power could I claim?
It was all due to the abundant blessings of the Celestial Worthy and the assembled gods.
How could I presume to trouble you for thanks?”

The Jade Emperor issued a decree ordering the gods of the Thunder Ministry to go separately and invite the Three Pure Ones, Four Imperial Sovereigns, Five Elders, Six Offices, Seven Primes, Eight Poles, Nine Luminaries, Ten Capitals, the thousand perfected ones, and the myriad sages to attend the gathering and join in thanking the Buddha for his grace.

He also commanded the Four Great Celestial Masters and the immortal maidens of the Nine Heavens to throw open the Golden Portal of the Jade Capital, the Precious Palace of the Great Mystery, and the Jade Hall of Grottoed Light; to seat the Tathagata in honor upon the seven-jeweled sacred dais; to arrange the ranks of seats; and to prepare dragon liver, phoenix marrow, jade nectar, and immortal peaches.

p.src: Before long there arrived the Jade-Purity Celestial Worthy of Primordial Beginning, the High-Purity Celestial Worthy of Numinous Treasure, the Great-Purity Celestial Worthy of the Way and Its Virtue, the Perfect Lords of the Five Breaths, the Star Lords of the Five Bushels, the Three Officials and Four Sages, the Perfect Lords of the Nine Luminaries, the Left Assistant and Right Supporter, the Heavenly Kings, Nezha, and every divinity of the mysterious void endowed with spiritual powers. They came beneath paired standards and twin banners and canopies, each bearing bright pearls and rare treasures, fruits of longevity and wondrous flowers. Presenting these before the Buddha, they bowed and said, “We are grateful for the Tathagata’s immeasurable Dharma power in subduing the demon monkey. The Great Celestial Worthy has graciously prepared a banquet and summoned us all here to offer our thanks. Would the Tathagata be pleased to give this gathering a name?” Accepting the gods’ request, the Tathagata said, “Since a name is desired, let it be called the Grand Assembly for Pacifying Heaven.” All the venerable immortals cried with one voice, “What an excellent name, ‘Grand Assembly for Pacifying Heaven’! What an excellent name, ‘Grand Assembly for Pacifying Heaven’!” When they had finished speaking, all took their appointed seats. Wine cups passed from hand to hand, flowers adorned their hair, and zithers were played: it was truly a splendid gathering. A poem bears witness to this. The poem says:

p.src: While all were joyfully enjoying the gathering, the Queen Mother appeared, leading a company of immortal maidens, celestial attendants, lovely women, and beauties who floated gracefully in dance before the Buddha. She bowed and said, “Earlier the demon monkey threw the Peach Banquet into disorder, and now the assembled immortals and Buddhas have together brought matters to a successful conclusion. Now, through the Tathagata’s mighty Dharma, the stubborn monkey has been forged in chains, and we joyfully celebrate the Grand Assembly for Pacifying Heaven. Having nothing else with which to express my thanks, I have washed my hands and personally plucked several peaches from the great trees to offer you.” Truly it was this:

p.src: Then the God of Longevity arrived. After paying his respects to the Jade Emperor, he also greeted the Tathagata and offered his thanks, saying, “When I first heard that the demon monkey had been taken by Laozi to the Tushita Palace to be refined, I thought peace would surely be restored, but unexpectedly he broke loose and rebelled again. Fortunately, the Tathagata skillfully subdued the monster. A banquet has been prepared in gratitude, and when I heard the news, I came at once. I have nothing else worthy to offer, so I present these purple lingzhi mushrooms, jasper herbs, emerald lotus roots, and golden elixir pills.” A poem says:

p.src: The Tathagata gladly accepted the gifts and thanked him. The God of Longevity took his seat, and once more the wine cups passed freely around. Then the Barefoot Immortal arrived. p.src: The Tathagata thanked him as well, then ordered Ananda and Kasyapa to gather up every offering before he turned to thank the Jade Emperor for the banquet. Everyone had drunk their fill. Just then, a celestial inspector came to report, “The Great Sage has stuck his head out.” The Buddha said, “Never mind, never mind.” From his sleeve he merely took out a paper talisman bearing six golden characters: “Om mani padme hum.” He handed it to Ananda and told him to paste it on the summit of the mountain. The venerable disciple accepted the talisman, carried it beyond the Gate of Heaven, and pasted it firmly onto a square stone atop the Mountain of Five Elements. At once the mountain rooted itself and every fissure sealed tight. The Great Sage could still breathe freely, and he could thrust out his hands and wriggle them about. Ananda returned and reported, “The talisman has been affixed.”

p.src: The Tathagata then took leave of the Jade Emperor and the assembled gods and departed beyond the Gate of Heaven with his two venerable disciples. Moved once more by compassion, he recited a true-word spell, summoned a local tutelary god to the Mountain of Five Elements, and ordered him to dwell there with the Five Directional Guardians and keep watch over the prisoner. Whenever he grew hungry, they were to give him iron pellets to eat; whenever he grew thirsty, they were to give him molten copper to drink. When the term of his calamity and punishment was fulfilled, someone would come to rescue him. Indeed:
